meta.title: Enterprise Analytics Platform Capability Rubric: GA4, Adobe Analytics, CJA, Amplitude

platforms.name: Google Analytics 4
platforms.notes: GA4 free + GA4 360 treated as one platform. 360 adds unsampled explorations (only when a query would exceed ~1B events; standard Explorations sample above 10M events), higher BigQuery export limits (standard is capped at 1M events/day daily export), subproperties & roll-up properties, Fresh Daily BigQuery export, higher cardinality limits, and SLAs. 360 retail starts at $50,000/year for 25M events/month, scaling toward ~$150,000/yr at high volume.

platforms.name: Adobe Analytics
platforms.notes: Select/Prime/Ultimate treated as one platform. Analysis Workspace, Attribution IQ, Anomaly Detection, Contribution Analysis. Contribution Analysis and hourly/weekly/monthly anomaly detection are gated above Select/Foundation tiers.

platforms.name: Customer Journey Analytics
platforms.notes: Adobe Experience Platform-based. Report-time processing, field-based (Select+) and graph-based (Prime+) stitching, AI Assistant, Data Insights Agent, Content Analytics add-on, Forecasting (Select+). HIPAA-ready.

platforms.name: Amplitude
platforms.notes: Starter(free)/Plus/Growth/Enterprise treated as one platform. Analytics, Experiment (Amplitude took over Statsig's brand/customers May 2026 after OpenAI's $1.1B acquisition — code without the founding team), CDP/Data, Session Replay, Amplitude AI (Ask Amplitude, Global Agent). Billed on MTUs + event volume with 1.2x overage.

meta.methodology: Built from vendor documentation (support.google.com, experienceleague.adobe.com, amplitude.com/docs), vendor release notes, and reputable independent comparisons (Vendr, Cardinal Path, InfoTrust), cross-referenced against help/docs rather than marketing pages. Support ratings reflect consultant judgment about real-world behavior including tier gating, add-ons, and implementation gotchas. Confidence reflects source strength and recency as of Jan 2026.

pillars.name: Data Collection & Ingestion
pillars.description: How each platform captures data across web, mobile, server, and offline sources, and how much taxonomy control it imposes.

capabilities.name: Web & Mobile SDK Coverage
capabilities.description: Breadth of first-party collection libraries determines implementation flexibility.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides a first-party web JavaScript SDK/tag for browser tracking

ga4.rationale: gtag.js and Google Tag Manager; also Firebase for apps.

aa.rationale: AppMeasurement.js (legacy) and Web SDK (alloy.js) via Edge Network; Web SDK is the recommended path for new customers.

cja.rationale: Uses Experience Platform Web SDK (alloy.js) sending to Edge Network / AEP datasets; can also reuse Adobe Analytics source connector.

amp.rationale: Browser SDK 2.x with built-in autocapture; also GTM/Segment integrations.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers native mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, and cross-platform frameworks (React Native, Flutter)

ga4.rationale: Firebase SDKs cover iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, Unity.

aa.rationale: Adobe Experience Platform Mobile SDK (iOS, Android; React Native and Flutter wrappers).

cja.rationale: Same AEP Mobile SDK feeding Edge Network/AEP; React Native and Flutter extensions available.

amp.rationale: iOS-Swift, Android-Kotlin, React Native, Flutter SDKs, all with autocapture support.

sub_capabilities.question: Auto-captures clicks, page views, and form interactions without upfront per-event tagging

ga4.rationale: Enhanced Measurement auto-collects page views, scrolls, outbound clicks, site search, form interactions, video engagement out of the box.

aa.rationale: Activity Map captures click data; but Adobe's model is fundamentally tag-and-map (eVars/props/events), so true codeless autocapture is limited vs GA4/Amplitude.

cja.rationale: CJA analyzes whatever is ingested into AEP; it has no independent autocapture layer — collection depends on Web SDK/other sources you configure.

amp.rationale: Autocapture (Browser SDK 2.10+) captures sessions, page views, clicks, form interactions, file downloads, attribution; element interactions require elementInteractions:true. Visual labeling works retroactively.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports server-side collection (Measurement Protocol, server-side tag manager, Edge Network, or HTTP API)

ga4.rationale: Measurement Protocol and server-side Google Tag Manager containers.

aa.rationale: Bulk Data Insertion API and Data Insertion API for server-side; Edge Network server-side forwarding.

cja.rationale: Edge Network server-side; AEP streaming/batch ingestion APIs and source connectors.

amp.rationale: HTTP V2 API, Batch API, and server-side SDKs (Node, Python, Java, Go, etc.).

sub_capabilities.question: Supports connected-TV/OTT and streaming-media measurement

ga4.rationale: No dedicated OTT/CTV SDK; video engagement events on web only. CTV must be piped via Measurement Protocol with custom work.

aa.rationale: Streaming Media Collection with OTT SDKs (Roku, tvOS, etc.).

cja.rationale: Streaming Media Collection now documented for CJA/Edge implementations.

amp.rationale: No dedicated OTT SDK; would require custom HTTP API integration.

capabilities.name: Data Sources, Offline & Warehouse Ingestion
capabilities.description: Ability to bring in CRM, offline, file, and warehouse data broadens analysis beyond digital.

sub_capabilities.question: Ingests offline/CRM/POS data via file upload or data import

ga4.rationale: Data Import (cost, item, user, offline event data) via CSV/SFTP; offline conversions via Measurement Protocol. Join keys limited.

aa.rationale: Data Sources and classifications/SAINT for offline enrichment; Customer Attributes for CRM traits.

cja.rationale: Core strength: ingests any online/offline dataset into AEP data lake (call-center, POS, CRM) and blends at person level.

amp.rationale: CSV import, HTTP API, and warehouse imports; profile/group properties.

sub_capabilities.question: Ingests data directly from cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks)

ga4.rationale: No warehouse-to-GA4 ingestion; GA4 is one-directional out to BigQuery. Data Import is file/API only.

aa.rationale: Adobe Analytics report suites cannot ingest from warehouses directly; you'd route via AEP/CJA instead.

cja.rationale: AEP source connectors for cloud storage/warehouses; Data Mirror (with CDC) for Snowflake/BigQuery/Databricks is rolling out.

amp.rationale: Warehouse-native import from Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift with append-only or CDC mirror sync;  Snowflake Native Amplitude queries data in place.

sub_capabilities.question: Enforces data governance at collection (validation, tracking plans, blocking bad data)

ga4.rationale: Minimal collection-time validation; no native tracking-plan enforcement. Bad events land as-is.

aa.rationale: Processing rules, VISTA rules, marketing-channel rules at collection time; report-suite governance.

cja.rationale: AEP schema enforcement (XDM), Data Prep validation, data governance labels/policies.

amp.rationale: Amplitude Data: tracking plans, taxonomy validation, observability, AI Data Assistant suggestions.

sub_capabilities.question: Uses an open/flexible event schema rather than a fixed taxonomy

ga4.rationale: Event + parameter model, open; but hard limits on custom dimensions/registered params.

aa.rationale: Fixed taxonomy of eVars, props, and success events that must be pre-allocated and mapped; the defining constraint of the classic model.

cja.rationale: Open XDM schema in AEP; eVars/props concept dropped in favor of arbitrary dimensions and report-time derived fields.

amp.rationale: Open event + property model with arbitrary user/event/group properties.

pillars.name: Identity & Profile Management
pillars.description: How platforms resolve users across devices/channels — the biggest architectural differentiator between web analytics and journey analytics.

capabilities.name: Cross-Device & Cross-Channel Identity
capabilities.description: Deterministic and graph-based stitching quality determines journey accuracy.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides deterministic cross-device stitching via a logged-in user ID

ga4.rationale: User-ID feature plus Google Signals; reporting identity blends User-ID, device, and modeled data.

aa.rationale: Cross-Device Analytics (CDA) with field-based stitching via the Experience Cloud ID and a declared person ID.

cja.rationale: Field-based stitching (Select+) rekeys events to a person ID across authenticated/unauthenticated events within a dataset.

amp.rationale: Amplitude ID merges anonymous device IDs to user IDs deterministically on login, including retroactive merge.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers identity-graph resolution across multiple identifiers/namespaces

ga4.rationale: No true identity graph; relies on User-ID + Google Signals modeling, not a configurable multi-namespace graph.

aa.rationale: Classic Adobe Analytics has no configurable identity graph; CDA stitching is single-key field-based.

cja.rationale: Graph-based stitching (Prime+) uses the AEP Identity Service graph to resolve a person ID across namespaces (email, phone, ECID); shares the graph with RTCDP/AJO.

amp.rationale: Amplitude resolves anonymous-to-known via merge but is not a multi-namespace identity graph like AEP's.

sub_capabilities.question: Binds anonymous history to a user retroactively on login (backfill)

ga4.rationale: User-ID associates future sessions; retroactive stitching of prior anonymous events is not reliably supported in the UI.

aa.rationale: Stitching happens going forward; classic AA does not retroactively rewrite historical anonymous hits at person level.

cja.rationale: Replay stitching reprocesses historical data to bind anonymous events to a person ID (lookback window/backfill per package).

amp.rationale: On merge, prior anonymous events are attributed to the resolved user; visual-labeled and autocaptured events also apply retroactively.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports account/household-level (B2B) identity analysis

ga4.rationale: No account/group entity; user- and session-scoped only.

aa.rationale: No native account-level roll-up of individuals; visitor-centric.

cja.rationale: CJA B2B Edition connects individuals to buying groups, accounts, and opportunities.

amp.rationale: Accounts add-on enables group/organization-level bucketing and analysis.

sub_capabilities.question: Works with first-party cookieless / consent-degraded environments via modeling

ga4.rationale: Consent Mode v2 with behavioral & conversion modeling to fill gaps when consent is denied.

aa.rationale: First-party server-side (CNAME) collection; but no equivalent to Google's conversion modeling.

cja.rationale: Edge Network first-party collection and AEP consent handling; person-based model less cookie-dependent.

amp.rationale: First-party SDK with server-side options; less reliant on third-party cookies but no ML consent modeling.

pillars.name: Data Modeling & Schema Flexibility
pillars.description: How dimensions, metrics, and transformations are defined — and whether changes apply retroactively.

capabilities.name: Custom Dimensions, Metrics & Transformations
capabilities.description: Governs analytical flexibility and how easily the model adapts after launch.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports calculated/derived metrics defined in-platform

ga4.rationale: Calculated metrics available (limited number per property); custom metrics via parameters.

aa.rationale: Calculated Metrics builder with segments, functions, containers — very mature.

cja.rationale: Calculated metrics plus report-time derived fields that transform data on the fly.

amp.rationale: Custom/computed metrics and formulas; derived properties.

sub_capabilities.question: Applies data transformations retroactively to historical data without reprocessing pipelines

ga4.rationale: Most config changes (custom dimensions, channel groups partially) are not fully retroactive; historical data largely fixed.

aa.rationale: Collection-time processing (processing rules, VISTA) is not retroactive; classifications and some report-time attribution are exceptions.

cja.rationale: Signature strength: report-time processing and derived fields transform data retroactively across all reporting without re-ingesting.

amp.rationale: Visual labeling and many transformations apply retroactively; data is event-stored and re-queried.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports lookups/classifications (SAINT-style enrichment) of dimension values

ga4.rationale: No SAINT equivalent; limited to data import joins on keys.

aa.rationale: Classifications / SAINT and Classification Rule Builder are core AA features.

cja.rationale: Lookup datasets and classifications supported via AEP + Analysis Workspace joins.

amp.rationale: Lookup tables and property enrichment supported.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides virtual report views/data views to reshape data per audience without new collection

ga4.rationale: 360 subproperties and roll-up properties act as filtered/aggregated views (at additional 50% event cost).

aa.rationale: Virtual Report Suites reshape and segment data without new collection.

cja.rationale: Data Views are the core reshaping layer — per-view components, attribution, session definitions, all report-time.

amp.rationale: Projects segment access but there's no equivalent report-time 'data view' reshaping layer per audience.

sub_capabilities.question: Handles high-cardinality dimensions without heavy sampling or '(other)' bucketing

ga4.rationale: Standard properties bucket high-cardinality values into '(other)'; 360 enables automatic custom tables to reduce this.

aa.rationale: Handles high-cardinality eVars well; unsampled by design.

cja.rationale: Processes full datasets without sampling in most workflows.

amp.rationale: Handles high-cardinality properties; some UI limits on group-by breadth.

pillars.name: Core Analytics & Exploration
pillars.description: Depth of self-serve analysis: segmentation, funnels, pathing, retention, and freeform exploration.

capabilities.name: Segmentation & Ad-hoc Exploration
capabilities.description: The workhorse of analysis — flexibility of segments and free-form workspace.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides a free-form drag-and-drop exploration workspace

ga4.rationale: Explorations module (free-form, funnel, path, cohort, segment overlap). Less powerful than Workspace/Amplitude.

aa.rationale: Analysis Workspace is the industry benchmark for free-form analysis.

cja.rationale: Same Analysis Workspace, extended to cross-channel data.

amp.rationale: Highly self-serve chart builder (Event Segmentation, funnels, etc.).

sub_capabilities.question: Supports sequential segmentation (event order, then/before/after logic)

ga4.rationale: Sequence segments in Explorations with step ordering and time constraints.

aa.rationale: Sequential segments with then/within logic, hit/visit/visitor containers.

cja.rationale: Same segmentation engine, person-scoped.

amp.rationale: Behavioral cohorts with sequence, order, and time-window conditions.

sub_capabilities.question: Runs unsampled analysis on large datasets in the UI

ga4.rationale: Standard Explorations sample above 10M events; 360 raises to ~1B and offers unsampled explorations only when a query would exceed 1B events. True unsampled requires BigQuery.

aa.rationale: Analysis Workspace is unsampled by default.

cja.rationale: Processes full datasets without sampling in standard workflows.

amp.rationale: Core analyses run on full data; some very large queries may use approximation but not GA-style sampling.

capabilities.name: Funnels, Pathing, Retention & Flow
capabilities.description: Behavioral analysis techniques where product-analytics tools historically lead.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports ordered and unordered funnel analysis with conversion windows

ga4.rationale: Funnel exploration with open/closed funnels and step ordering.

aa.rationale: Fallout visualization with flexible step logic.

cja.rationale: Same fallout/flow tooling, cross-channel.

amp.rationale: Best-in-class funnels with ordered/unordered/any-order, conversion windows, and micro-segmentation.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides open-ended path/journey analysis (next/previous step, Sankey/flow)

ga4.rationale: Path exploration (forward and backward from a node).

aa.rationale: Flow visualization with next/previous nodes.

cja.rationale: Flow plus Journey Canvas for cross-channel journeys.

amp.rationale: Pathfinder and Journeys for open-ended path discovery.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers advanced retention/cohort analysis (N-day, unbounded, rolling, bracket)

ga4.rationale: Cohort exploration with limited retention criteria.

aa.rationale: Cohort tables in Workspace with rolling/retention/churn options.

cja.rationale: Same cohort tables, cross-channel.

amp.rationale: Deepest retention analysis: N-day, unbounded, bracketed, rolling; retention drivers.

sub_capabilities.question: Retroactively analyzes funnels/segments defined after data was collected

ga4.rationale: Explorations query historical events retroactively within retention limits.

aa.rationale: Segments/fallout apply retroactively to collected data.

cja.rationale: Report-time model is inherently retroactive.

amp.rationale: All events retained and re-queryable; funnels/cohorts fully retroactive.

pillars.name: Attribution & Marketing Analytics
pillars.description: Multi-touch attribution, channel modeling, and statistical diagnostics — where Adobe and GA4 lead over product-analytics tools.

capabilities.name: Attribution Modeling
capabilities.description: Rule-based and algorithmic attribution for marketing measurement.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers data-driven/algorithmic attribution beyond simple rules

ga4.rationale: Data-Driven Attribution is the default model, using ML across paths; also last-click and Google Ads-preferred.

aa.rationale: Attribution IQ algorithmic model uses the Harsanyi Dividend from cooperative game theory, a generalization of the Shapley value solution.

cja.rationale: Same Attribution IQ models plus cross-channel attribution and incrementality.

amp.rationale: Amplitude does multi-touch and first/last-touch attribution but lacks a mature algorithmic marketing-attribution model comparable to DDA/Attribution IQ.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides a broad set of rule-based multi-touch models (linear, U-shaped, time-decay, custom, comparable in one view)

ga4.rationale: GA4 deprecated most rule-based models; effectively DDA + last-click (paid/organic) remain.

aa.rationale: Ten models incl. custom, side-by-side in the Attribution IQ panel; any metric, any lookback.

cja.rationale: Same Attribution IQ model set, applied cross-channel.

amp.rationale: First/last/linear multi-touch available but marketing-channel focus is shallower than Adobe.

sub_capabilities.question: Includes marketing-channel attribution with configurable channel rules

ga4.rationale: Default and custom channel groups; deep Google Ads/DV360/SA360 linking.

aa.rationale: Marketing Channel processing rules (collection-time).

cja.rationale: Marketing channels via source connector or report-time derived fields.

amp.rationale: Channel/attribution via UTM and marketing analytics module, less rich than Adobe.

capabilities.name: Statistical Diagnostics
capabilities.description: Anomaly detection, contribution/root-cause, and forecasting for proactive insight.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides automated anomaly detection with statistical confidence bands

ga4.rationale: Insights anomaly detection in reports; less configurable.

aa.rationale: Anomaly Detection with hourly/daily/weekly/monthly granularity and seasonality; hourly+ gated above Select/Foundation.

cja.rationale: Same anomaly detection engine cross-channel.

amp.rationale: Anomaly detection and automated monitors/alerts.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers contribution/root-cause analysis to explain an anomaly

ga4.rationale: No dedicated contribution-analysis engine; manual investigation.

aa.rationale: Contribution Analysis (Cramér's V + Pearson residuals) on top 50,000 items/dimension; token-limited and excludes Select/Foundation tiers.

cja.rationale: Contribution Analysis available; Data Insights Agent adds AI-assisted root-cause.

amp.rationale: Root Cause / anomaly explanation via AI Agents and impact analysis.

sub_capabilities.question: Includes native time-series forecasting inside dashboards

ga4.rationale: No native forecasting in UI beyond predictive metrics; forecasting done in BigQuery/BQML.

aa.rationale: No general-purpose time-series forecasting in Analysis Workspace (predictive is limited).

cja.rationale: Forecasting (Select+) uses Meta's open-source Prophet model for time-series prediction with a 95% prediction interval inside freeform tables/line charts.

amp.rationale: Forecasting on metrics and predictive charts.

pillars.name: AI & Machine Learning
pillars.description: Predictive metrics, predictive audiences, and natural-language/generative AI assistants.

capabilities.name: Predictive Metrics & Audiences
capabilities.description: Native churn/purchase/LTV prediction and predictive segment creation.

sub_capabilities.question: Ships native predictive metrics (churn, purchase probability, predicted revenue)

ga4.rationale: Purchase probability, churn probability, predicted revenue — but require, in the last 28 days over a seven-day period, at least 1,000 returning users who triggered the condition and at least 1,000 who did not, plus purchase events, to stay eligible.

aa.rationale: No native churn/purchase-probability scoring in classic AA.

cja.rationale: No native GA propensity metric; churn/conversion scoring comes from AEP Customer AI (separate) ingested into CJA.

amp.rationale: Predictive cohorts/scores (e.g., likelihood to convert/churn) available on higher tiers.

sub_capabilities.question: Builds predictive audiences that can be activated downstream

ga4.rationale: Predictive audiences (e.g., 'Likely 7-day purchasers') auto-shared to Google Ads/DV360/SA360.

aa.rationale: Not natively; requires Adobe Audience Manager/RTCDP.

cja.rationale: Behavioral/predictive audiences (with AEP Customer AI scores) activatable via RTCDP.

amp.rationale: Predictive cohorts sync to destinations via Amplitude CDP.

capabilities.name: Generative & Natural-Language AI
capabilities.description: Conversational querying, AI-generated insights, and content AI.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers a natural-language / conversational query assistant

ga4.rationale: Gemini-powered insights in GA4 and via Gemini Enterprise connectors for NL querying.

aa.rationale: AI Assistant available for Adobe Analytics (NL product knowledge + some analysis).

cja.rationale: AI Assistant (all tiers) plus Data Insights Agent (generative NL, builds Workspace visualizations); Data Insights Agent free for a limited time then needs Agent Orchestrator license.

amp.rationale: Ask Amplitude and Global Agent (via Amazon Bedrock LLM) create charts and answer questions in NL.

sub_capabilities.question: Auto-generates written insights/summaries of report data

ga4.rationale: Automated & custom Insights narratives.

aa.rationale: Intelligent Alerts and generated insights/captions.

cja.rationale: Intelligent Captions translate visualizations to NL summaries; auto-generated insights.

amp.rationale: AI-generated summaries/insights and notebooks.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides content-performance AI (attribute-level content analytics)

ga4.rationale: No content-attribute AI; page/content reports only.

aa.rationale: No content-featurization AI in classic AA.

cja.rationale: Content Analytics uses AI featurization to break assets into attributes and measure impact; add-on (rollout Mar 2025), English-only, and no longer licensable as a CJA add-on as of Feb 2026 (standalone purchase required).

amp.rationale: No content-attribute AI equivalent.

pillars.name: Experimentation & Personalization
pillars.description: Native A/B testing, feature flags, and personalization — a decisive Amplitude advantage.

capabilities.name: Native Experimentation
capabilities.description: Whether the platform can run and analyze experiments itself.

sub_capabilities.question: Includes a native A/B testing engine with a statistics engine

ga4.rationale: GA4 has no native A/B engine; Google Optimize was sunset in 2023. Relies on third-party tools.

aa.rationale: Adobe's testing lives in Adobe Target (A4T integration), a separate product; AA only analyzes results.

cja.rationale: CJA can evaluate lift/confidence of experiments from any connected data source but doesn't run tests itself.

amp.rationale: Amplitude Experiment: full A/B engine with sequential testing, T-tests, CUPED, multi-armed bandits, mutual exclusion groups. Note: Amplitude took over Statsig's brand/customers in May 2026 (code without the founding engineering team), a support-continuity risk to monitor.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides native feature flags / feature management

ga4.rationale: No feature-flag capability.

aa.rationale: No feature-flag capability.

cja.rationale: No feature-flag capability.

amp.rationale: Enterprise-grade feature flags, client/server-side, local/remote evaluation, payloads; unlimited flags even on free tier.

sub_capabilities.question: Analyzes experiment results using the platform's own behavioral metrics/segments

ga4.rationale: No native experiment analysis.

aa.rationale: Analytics for Target (A4T) analyzes Target tests with AA metrics/segments.

cja.rationale: Can evaluate experiment lift/confidence from any connected dataset.

amp.rationale: Experiment Results ties test analysis to full behavioral data; can bring your own flags.

pillars.name: Qualitative & Experience Analytics
pillars.description: Session replay, heatmaps, and frustration signals that explain the 'why' behind metrics.

capabilities.name: Session Replay & Heatmaps
capabilities.description: Visual behavioral analytics — historically a gap for analytics suites.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers native session replay for web and mobile

ga4.rationale: No native session replay.

aa.rationale: No native session replay (Adobe positions this via partners).

cja.rationale: No native session replay.

amp.rationale: Native Session Replay for web and mobile, integrated with charts/funnels; sampling & targeted capture.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides heatmaps / zone/click analysis

ga4.rationale: No native heatmaps.

aa.rationale: Activity Map provides click/link overlays (a limited heatmap).

cja.rationale: No native heatmaps.

amp.rationale: Heatmaps and Zoning insights (click, selector, scroll).

sub_capabilities.question: Detects frustration signals (rage clicks, dead clicks, errors)

ga4.rationale: No frustration-signal detection.

aa.rationale: No frustration-signal detection.

cja.rationale: No frustration-signal detection.

amp.rationale: Session Replay Agent surfaces rage clicks, dead clicks, form abandonment, console/network errors.

pillars.name: Activation & Ecosystem
pillars.description: Ad-platform integrations, native CDP, and audience activation to downstream systems.

capabilities.name: Ad Platform & Ecosystem Integrations
capabilities.description: Depth of native connections to ad and marketing platforms.

sub_capabilities.question: Has deep native integrations with major ad platforms

ga4.rationale: Best-in-class for Google stack: Google Ads, DV360, SA360; audience sharing built in. Non-Google (Meta/TikTok) requires third-party.

aa.rationale: Integrations via Adobe Advertising and Experience Cloud; not as turnkey for non-Adobe ad platforms.

cja.rationale: Activation via RTCDP to many ad/marketing destinations.

amp.rationale: 65+ turnkey integrations incl. Google Ads, Meta, TikTok via Amplitude CDP.

sub_capabilities.question: Includes native CDP capabilities (audience building + activation)

ga4.rationale: Audiences exist but no true CDP; activation limited to Google ecosystem.

aa.rationale: CDP is a separate product (Adobe RTCDP), not part of AA.

cja.rationale: Built on AEP; tightly integrated with RTCDP for profiles and activation (though RTCDP is a distinct license).

amp.rationale: Amplitude CDP built in: identity resolution, governance, audience syncing without a separate tool.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports reverse-ETL / audience activation to CRM, email, push

ga4.rationale: No general reverse-ETL; activation confined to Google destinations.

aa.rationale: Not natively; via RTCDP/Audience Manager.

cja.rationale: RTCDP destinations catalog + Journey Optimizer/Campaign for activation.

amp.rationale: Amplitude Activation syncs cohorts to email/push/ads; supports reverse-ETL patterns with Hightouch etc.

pillars.name: Data Export & Warehousing
pillars.description: Raw event export, BI connectivity, and warehouse interoperability — critical for enterprise data teams.

capabilities.name: Raw Event Export & Warehouse Interop
capabilities.description: Whether you own and can export raw, unsampled event data.

sub_capabilities.question: Exports raw, event-level data to a cloud data warehouse

ga4.rationale: Free native BigQuery export — the platform's standout feature. Standard daily export capped at 1M events/day; exceed it consistently and the daily export pauses without backfill. 360 removes the cap and adds Fresh Daily.

aa.rationale: Data Feeds deliver raw, unsampled, hit-level clickstream to cloud storage; Data Warehouse for aggregated exports.

cja.rationale: AEP Data Access API and Destinations export raw event/row-level data; Full Table Export is the evolution of Data Warehouse.

amp.rationale: Recurring event + merged-ID export to Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, S3, Kinesis; also raw Export API.

sub_capabilities.question: Delivers raw export without punitive row/event caps on the base license

ga4.rationale: Standard tier's 1M-events/day daily-export cap is a hard gotcha for high-traffic sites; streaming export is uncapped but best-effort with incomplete attribution intraday.

aa.rationale: Data Feeds process unlimited rows per request.

cja.rationale: Row-level export of all ingested data; subject to AEP guardrails not punitive caps.

amp.rationale: Export scales with your contracted volume; no artificial daily cap like GA4 free.

sub_capabilities.question: Connects natively to major BI tools (Looker, Tableau, Power BI)

ga4.rationale: Looker Studio native; Tableau/Power BI via BigQuery or connectors.

aa.rationale: Report Builder (Excel) and API; BI via data feeds.

cja.rationale: BI via AEP Query Service (PSQL interface) and exports.

amp.rationale: Warehouse exports feed any BI; dashboards native.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides SQL access to the underlying event data

ga4.rationale: Full SQL via BigQuery (nested/UNNEST schema learning curve).

aa.rationale: No SQL over AA data directly; must export to a warehouse first.

cja.rationale: AEP Query Service offers SQL access to the data lake (Data Distiller for advanced).

amp.rationale: Snowflake Native Amplitude and warehouse exports enable SQL; no in-product SQL editor for core analysis.

pillars.name: Privacy, Consent & Governance
pillars.description: Compliance posture: consent, residency, certifications, HIPAA/BAA, retention, and access control.

capabilities.name: Compliance & Certifications
capabilities.description: Regulatory readiness that gates use in healthcare, government, and the EU.

sub_capabilities.question: Integrates with consent management and honors consent signals

ga4.rationale: Consent Mode v2, integrations with OneTrust/Cookiebot; models conversions when consent denied.

aa.rationale: Consent handling via Edge/AEP and tag-based CMP integrations.

cja.rationale: AEP consent policies and data governance labels enforce consent.

amp.rationale: Consent controls in SDK/replay; CMP integrations.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports HIPAA compliance with a signed BAA

ga4.rationale: Google does not sign a BAA for GA; not usable with PHI. Server-side stripping only mitigates risk.

aa.rationale: Adobe Analytics is NOT HIPAA-ready per Adobe.

cja.rationale: CJA is HIPAA-ready; AEP/CJA covered under Adobe's SOC 2 + HIPAA scope, with BAA and Healthcare Shield options.

amp.rationale: HIPAA compliance and BAA available on Enterprise plan.

sub_capabilities.question: Holds FedRAMP authorization for government use

ga4.rationale: Google Cloud/Gemini via Vertex hold FedRAMP High; GA4 itself is not the typical FedRAMP vehicle — validate scope.

aa.rationale: Adobe Analytics is not FedRAMP-authorized (FedRAMP applies to specific Adobe gov products).

cja.rationale: CJA/AEP not FedRAMP-authorized as of early 2026 (holds SOC 2, ISO, HIPAA, IRAP for some regions).

amp.rationale: No FedRAMP authorization.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers regional data residency (EU/US/APAC)

ga4.rationale: Limited residency control; data processed in Google's global infrastructure — a repeated EU DPA concern.

aa.rationale: Report-suite data center selection (Americas/EU/APAC).

cja.rationale: AEP sandbox/region selection for residency.

amp.rationale: EU and US data residency; residency options on Enterprise.

sub_capabilities.question: Automates right-to-be-forgotten / DSAR deletion requests

ga4.rationale: User Deletion API; retention controls (2–14 months standard).

aa.rationale: Adobe Privacy Service handles access/deletion requests.

cja.rationale: AEP Privacy Service; GDPR deletions propagate to data lake, typically within 7 days.

amp.rationale: Privacy/deletion API and DSAR handling; profile deletion via privacy@amplitude.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides granular per-dataset/per-property data retention controls

ga4.rationale: Only 2 or 14 months for standard; 360 adds up to 50 months. Coarse controls.

aa.rationale: Configurable retention per contract/report suite.

cja.rationale: Rolling data window per connection; dataset-level TTL in AEP.

amp.rationale: Retention by tier (1yr Starter/Plus, 2yr Growth, unlimited Enterprise); custom on Enterprise.

pillars.name: Administration, Developer Experience & Commercial
pillars.description: Enterprise operations, APIs, access control, and licensing economics.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Administration & Access
capabilities.description: Multi-tenant structure, RBAC, SSO/SCIM, and audit.

sub_capabilities.question: Supports roll-up / cross-property reporting across business units

ga4.rationale: 360 roll-up properties (up to 200 source properties) and subproperties; both at additional 50% event cost.

aa.rationale: Global/rollup report suites.

cja.rationale: Connections combine multiple datasets across BUs at person level.

amp.rationale: Portfolio analysis (higher tiers) and multi-project structure.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides SSO/SAML and SCIM user provisioning

ga4.rationale: SSO via Google identity; enterprise SSO through Google Workspace/Cloud Identity.

aa.rationale: Adobe Admin Console SSO/SAML and user sync.

cja.rationale: Same Adobe Admin Console SSO/SAML/user sync.

amp.rationale: SSO on Growth+; SCIM provisioning on Growth/Enterprise (SSO prerequisite). Gated behind higher tiers.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides fine-grained role-based access control and audit logs

ga4.rationale: Property/account roles; 360 subproperties enable data-level access separation. Audit via change history.

aa.rationale: Admin Console RBAC, component/segment governance, audit logs.

cja.rationale: AEP attribute-based access control, object-level permissions, and audit.

amp.rationale: Org/project permissions; full custom RBAC only on Enterprise; no native idle-user report.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers a contractual uptime SLA and enterprise support/TAM

ga4.rationale: SLAs and support only on GA4 360; free tier has no SLA or dedicated support.

aa.rationale: Enterprise SLAs and support/TAM standard.

cja.rationale: Enterprise SLAs and support standard.

amp.rationale: Dedicated support, CSM, and custom SLAs on Enterprise only.

sub_capabilities.question: Exposes public reporting, admin, and data-import APIs

ga4.rationale: Data API, Admin API, Measurement Protocol, Data Import.

aa.rationale: Analytics 2.0 Reporting API, admin APIs, ingestion APIs.

cja.rationale: CJA APIs plus full AEP API surface (ingestion, query, privacy).

amp.rationale: Export, Dashboard REST, Taxonomy, Behavioral Cohort, Identify APIs.

sub_capabilities.question: Provides Terraform / infrastructure-as-code provisioning

ga4.rationale: No official Terraform provider for GA4 config (some community modules).

aa.rationale: No official Terraform provider.

cja.rationale: No official Terraform provider; API-driven config.

amp.rationale: No official Terraform provider; API/SDK-driven.

capabilities.name: Commercial & Licensing
capabilities.description: Pricing model, free tier, and cost predictability.

sub_capabilities.question: Offers a genuinely usable free tier

ga4.rationale: GA4 free is fully featured for most SMBs; the primary reason for its ubiquity.

aa.rationale: No free tier; enterprise contract only.

cja.rationale: No free tier; enterprise AEP-based contract.

amp.rationale: Starter free plan: 10K MTUs / ~2M events, session replay, unlimited feature flags, web experimentation, and AI — unusually generous.

sub_capabilities.question: Has predictable, transparent pricing

ga4.rationale: 360 moved to usage-based pricing with a retail start of $50,000/year for 25M events/month, scaling toward ~$150,000/yr at high volume; quotes are otherwise opaque and volume-driven.

aa.rationale: Custom enterprise pricing; opaque and negotiation-driven.

cja.rationale: AEP + CJA licensing is complex and opaque, with add-ons (Content Analytics, Agent Orchestrator).

amp.rationale: MTU + event dual billing with 1.2x overage; Plus is public ($49/mo billed annually, scaling to 300K MTUs) but Growth/Enterprise opaque; median annual contract ~$63,720 (Vendr, n=358).
